paragraphs: Leo and May sat on the steps of the library at lunchtime. The steps were in the shade, so it was cool there. Leo had a blue leaflet in his hand. "Look, May! There is a sailing day for children," he said. "I like boats, but I have never tried sailing," said May. "I would love to try it. Would you come with me?" asked Leo. "Certainly! When is it?" asked May.

"On Sunday at two o'clock," said Leo. Leo read from the leaflet. "Come to the sailing club at the pier." "Our manager will meet you at the gate." "It is a day for beginners." "Please wear a hat, and bring water." "The club is open every day except Monday," he said. "Is the training free?" asked May. "Yes, it is free for beginners," said Leo.

"Sunday is good for me," said May. "On Saturday morning, I have violin training." "Do you enjoy playing the violin?" asked Leo. "I love it, especially slow songs," said May. "I practice every day, but I do not have to practice on Sunday." "Do you like drawing boats?" "I like drawing them," said Leo, "but I want to sail in a real boat." "That sounds like a great plan," said May.

"How do we get to the pier?" asked May. "We take the bus from the school," said Leo. "It takes twenty minutes, and the bus stop is next to the pier." "Let's meet at the school bus stop at one o'clock," said May. "Then we will arrive early, and we can look at the boats first." "Good idea," said Leo. "I will ask Mom tonight, and she will sign the note," he said. "My mom works in the library, so I will ask her today," said May.

Lunchtime ended, and the children stood up. "See you on Sunday at one o'clock," said May. Leo took a pen and drew a small boat on the leaflet. "This is our boat," he said, "and it needs a name." "Let's call it the Green Flag," said May. They both laughed, and they walked to class.

sentences.text: Leo and May sat on the steps of the library at lunchtime.
